note: Source has plural 'their kings'; Arabic renders singular 'their king'.
Source negates the giving (God has not given you such things); Arabic affirms 'your God has given you', reversing the sense.
Omits 'for each ancestral house' (לְבֵית אָב); says one prince per tribe only.
Adds 'no longer/again' (لم يعودوا) not in source's 'they did not say'.
Hebrew 'they had just posted/stationed the guards' rendered as 'they had awakened the guards' — different action.
Reverses negation: 'I will not send and inform you' becomes rhetorical 'will I not send?'; omits the 'but if not, I will tell you' clause.
Rhetorical question ('Have I today begun to inquire of God for him?') turned into a plain statement ('Today I began to inquire').
Omits the place name Nachon ('to Nachon'); says only that Saul had indeed arrived.
Source says David rejected/spurned the enemies of Yahweh; Arabic says he made them blaspheme against him, adding a new idea and reversing the agent.
Second door's 'two hangings/curtains' (קלעים) rendered as 'two boards', losing distinction from first door's side-panels.
'turned their heart backward' rendered as 'turned their hearts to the truth', reversing the meaning
Source says Solomon came TO the high place in Gibeon; Arabic says he came FROM the high place to Jerusalem, reversing direction.
Omits 'according to their divisions' and 'for the priests and for the Levites'.
Person change: 'we ate and were satisfied' instead of 'the people ate and were satisfied'.
Object 'them' (the cooked food) omitted; 'hurried to' replaces 'carried/brought to' the people.
Last clause says the people of Jerusalem left the city to the Broad Wall, instead of they fortified/restored Jerusalem as far as the wall.
Adds 'dwelling' and renders 'in Judah and in Benjamin' as 'from Judah in Benjamin'.
Final clause changes 'I asked leave' to passive 'permission was sought', omitting the speaker.
Adds 'wheat' to 'heaps'; source says only heaps.
Omits 'on this account' (עַל כָּכָה) in 'what they saw'; adds gloss 'i.e., the lot'.
Reverses negation: source says 'you did not see calamity,' Arabic says 'you saw the blow'
Source is a statement; Arabic turns both clauses into rhetorical questions.
Changes 'it became a witness' to 'I became a witness' and 'to my face' to 'my face testifies against me'.
Renders final phrase as 'his vengeance' instead of 'while he is eating/his food'; adds vengeance and omits eating/food.
Hebrew 'days of my youth/prime' rendered as 'days of my winter', changing the idea
Changes 'by their instruction he seals' to 'he seals their instruction,' omitting the means idea.
Omits 'my arrow' and applies 'without transgression' to the speaker rather than the arrow.
Adds 'more' and changes 'from my sin' to 'more than my sin.'
Adds 'effeminate' (الْمُخَنَّثِينَ) not present in the source's 'consecrated.'
Renders 'upon it' as 'around him'; changes preposition and pronoun.
Object pronoun changed: 'cleared them' is rendered 'purifies it'.
Adds 'land' as object and 'vegetation' not present in source.
Adds 'himself' as object of 'blesses'; source has the greedy man blessing/scorning Yahweh, not himself.
Adds "إلى الأبد" (and forever), an idea not in the source's "from of old."
Imperative 'deliver them' changed into a rhetorical question 'Will they escape by iniquity?'
Adds 'upon them' to 'their wounds were,' which is not in the source.
Relative clause refers to the proud rather than the pits, saying the people are not according to your law.
Predicate 'is better' replaced by 'penetrates to the heart'; the comparison 'better than' is lost.
Omits that the oppressors are children/babes; renders the predicate as 'tyrannize' instead.
Adds 'والأكياس' (and the bags), which is not in the source list.
Negation 'without bowing' (בלתי כרע) rendered as 'except that they fall' (إلا أن يخروا), reversing the sense.
Omits 'from the city' (מֵעִיר) modifying the castle of strangers.
Second person 'you have seen / you do not observe' changed to third person 'he saw / he did not keep'.
Omits 'your principalities have fallen' (מַרְאֲשׁוֹתֵיכֶם); only the crown of majesty is mentioned.
Hebrew 'וְחִלֵּלוּ' (they will defile/profane) rendered as 'they will enjoy its fruit' — meaning changed.
'Wanderers who cause him to wander' rendered as 'emptiers who empty him', losing the staggering/wandering idea.
Subject changed: 'They did these to you' instead of 'I will do these to you.'
Final clause changed from 'her scum is in the fire' to 'let the fire devour her scum.'
Arabic has dual 'two posts' where source reads singular 'the post of the entrance'.
Omits 'chief of the governors' (רב סגנין); Arabic only says chief over all the wise men of Babylon.
Omits the possessive 'my' in 'my God'; Arabic says only 'with God'.
Source says 'like a lion'; Arabic says 'like a roar', omitting the lion image.
Omits the phrase 'from before the garment' (מִמּוּל שַׂלְמָה) modifying the stripping of the robe.
Rhetorical question reversed: Greek expects 'no' ('he is not going... is he?'), Arabic 'أليس' expects 'yes'.
Adds 'tried/attempted' (حاول) where source states he reconciled/set them at one.
Adds 'the human messengers, not the angels', an interpretive idea not in the source (which says 'the messengers/angels').
Adds 'and your ordinances' (وفرائضك), a distinct idea not in the source.
